title: Spinach, frozen, cooked with butter or margarine

content.title: About
content.content: Frozen spinach is a leafy vegetable that is blanched, cooled and flash‑frozen shortly after harvest. Cooking it with butter or margarine adds a smooth flavor and helps absorb fat‑soluble vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: When frozen quickly after picking, spinach retains most of its vitamins and minerals.
Blanching before freezing kills most bacteria and preserves the bright green color.
Spinach belongs to the Amaranth family and is a close relative of Swiss chard.
In the United States frozen spinach is a common ingredient in casseroles, lasagnas and smoothies.
Spinach is rich in lutein, which supports eye health.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Source of vitamin A and beta‑carotene
items.content: Supports vision, immune function and skin.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron is needed for oxygen transport in the blood, especially important in plant‑based diets.

items.title: High in folate
items.content: Folate is involved in DNA synthesis and is crucial during pregnancy.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin protect the eyes from age‑related changes.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Spinach contains oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Food allergies
items.content: Rarely, some people may experience an allergic reaction to spinach.

items.title: Sodium content in prepared dishes
items.content: If butter or margarine is salted, consider the overall sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Thaw the spinach and quickly sauté it with butter or margarine, then add to soups, sauces, omelets, casseroles, or use as a filling for pies. A small amount of fat helps retain nutrients.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen spinach in a freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. Once thawed, use within 1–2 days and store in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
